question: The income of Raman is ₹44,200. He saves 31% of his income. If his income increases by 22% and expenditure increases by 50%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Let Income = 100, Savings = 31, then Expenditure = 69

New Income = 100 + 22 = 122 | New Expenditure = 69 × 1.5 = 103.5

New Savings = 122 − 103.5 = 18.5

Change in Savings = 31 − 18.5 = 12.5 decrease

1 unit = 44200/100 = 442 | Decrease = 12.5 × 442 = ₹5,525

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹5,525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹44,200

Initial Savings % = 31%

Income increase = 22%

Expenditure increase = 50%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e2f01174600f4b25765089a3c534e0facc8715d43a6cf10ea873633335b5443.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = 31% of 44,200 = 0.31 × 44,200 = ₹13,702

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 44,200 − 13,702 = ₹30,498

⇒ New Income = 44,200 + 22% of 44,200 = 44,200 × 1.22 = ₹53,924

⇒ New Expenditure = 30,498 + 50% of 30,498 = 30,498 × 1.5 = ₹45,747

⇒ New Savings = 53,924 − 45,747 = ₹8,177

⇒ Change in Savings = 13,702 − 8,177 = ₹5,525 decrease

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹5,525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income Formula

Income = Expenditure + Savings. This is the fundamental equation for all household budget problems.

Percentage Change

New Value = Old Value × (100 + Change%)/100. If Change% is negative, it represents a decrease.

Savings Rate

Savings Rate = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. It measures the portion of income not spent on consumption.
